messages.subject: 2nd-order CFA model identification
parts:
Hi everyone, 


From my understanding the model that I have is over-identified at the first-order and just-identified at the second-order (I used marker indicator).   It implies that the second-order CFA is not over-identified and thus SE cannot be calculated/trusted.  However, lavaan package seems to give me an reasonable SE.  Could anyone explain why the result is like this? Could I interpret the significance of the loadings based on the output? 



Best,

Xiaomeng

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: 2nd-order CFA model identification
parts: It implies that the second-order CFA is not over-identified and thus SE cannot be calculated/trusted.

No, under-identification would prevent valid SEs from being calculated.  Just-identification means you can trust your results, but they are statistically equivalent to a CFA with only the 3 freely covarying first-order factors.
Could I interpret the significance of the loadings based on the output?

The same way you interpret first-order loadings: how many units the indicator changes for each 1-unit increase in its common factor.
